title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In the 'équation des lacets' manuscripts (pp. 293-650 of the continuation of La Longue Marche), Grothendieck studies pairs (multiplier p = 2σ+1 ∈ Ẑ*, element ξ or g in π̂_{0,3} = F̂_2). These are the Grothendieck-Teichmüller-type equations: ρ is the order-3 automorphism cyclically permuting the three loops ℓ_0, ℓ_1, ℓ_∞, and p = χ(u) is the cyclotomic multiplier. To get information about the solutions, he pushes the equation to the image of π̂_{0,3} in SL(2,Ẑ)', via the congruence subgroup π(2) = Ker(SL(2,Ẑ)' → SL(2,Z/2)). This subgroup is generated topologically by ℓ_0 = [[1,2],[0,1]] and ℓ_1 = [[1,0],[2,1]], and ρ acts there by conjugation by an order-3 element.

What the previous page establishes.
- The image of ξ has one of two forms:
  - (A) ξ = λρ(λ)^{-1};
  - (B) ξ = λ ℓ_0^{-1} ρ(λ)^{-1}, with λ = (a b; c d).
- Writing ξ = (A B; C D), the loop equation (93) reduces to p·D = ±1:
  - in case A, with D = c²+cd+d²;
  - in case B, with D = 3c²+3cd+d², giving pD = −1 (formulas (99)-(101)).

This page, step 1 (closing the case analysis). Mod 3 one has 3c²+3cd+d² ≡ d², so this form takes only the values 0 and 1 mod 3. Since D must be a unit, D ≡ 1 (3), and pD = −1 then forces p ≡ −1 (3), equivalently σ ≡ −1 (3) (formula (102)).

Combined with case A, where D = c²+cd+d² ≡ (c−d)² mod 3 and pD = 1, he concludes:
- the 'coboundary' case ξ = λρ(λ)^{-1} occurs exactly when p = χ(u) ≡ 1 (3), i.e. σ ≡ 0 (3);
- the twisted case ξ = λℓ_0^{-1}ρ(λ)^{-1} occurs exactly when p ≡ −1 (3), i.e. σ ≡ −1 (3).

This page, step 2 (Remark 1). Working in SL(2,Ẑ)', or rather in π(2)' or the image of π̂_{0,3}, put ξ in 'primitive form' (94). Then the equation (**) in ξ (cf. (68)) becomes an anodyne condition on λ = (a b; c d): pD = 1, where
- D = c²+cd+d² in the first case;
- D = −(c²+cd+d²) in the second.
The correction from 3c²+3cd+d² to −(c²+cd+d²) is legitimate: both forms have discriminant −3, class number 1, and the substitution d ↦ d−c carries d²+3cd+3c² to c²+cd+d²; the sign is absorbed by the convention pD = −1. So if p is fixed in advance, the condition is just that D be a unit of Ẑ.

The next page completes the point. From ξ one recovers D, hence p, then σ, then h_0 = ℓ_0^{-σ}ξ, then g_0, g and ρ. He checks invariance under ξ ↦ ℓ_0^{-α}ξℓ_1^{α}, which leaves D unchanged. He also warns that the image in SL(2,Ẑ)' alone determines p only up to sign.

In modern terms: this is the image of a GT-type (hexagon/loop) equation in the congruence completion of the modular group. Twisted ρ-conjugacy in SL2 is governed by the norm form of the Eisenstein integers, Ẑ[ω]; ω is the eigenvalue of the order-3 element. The cyclotomic multiplier is then read off as the inverse of a norm, up to sign. The case split by p mod 3 is a split by the class of ξ in twisted-conjugacy classes.
errors: No mathematical error detected. The mod-3 argument (D ≡ d² ∈ {0,1}, D a unit hence D ≡ 1, pD = −1 hence p ≡ −1 (3)) is correct.

The crossed-out D = 3c²+3cd+d² versus the inserted −(c²+d²+cd) is not a contradiction. The two binary forms of discriminant −3 are SL2(Z)-equivalent via d ↦ d−c. The rewrite presumably reflects a change of the parametrizing λ (λ' vs λ), but the page does not make this explicit, so it is a small expository gap.

ideas.what: Reduction of the loop (hexagon-type) equation for (p, ξ) to the congruence image of π̂_{0,3} = Γ̂(2) in SL(2,Ẑ), yielding the scalar condition pD = ±1
ideas.modern_name: Image of GT-hat / Galois action in the congruence completion of SL2(Z) (Γ(2) level)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld 1990 and Ihara for the GT setting; images of GT in congruence quotients are discussed by Lochak-Schneps, Nakamura and others
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse or the published Longue Marche excerpts as far as I know (unsure)

ideas.what: Twisted ρ-conjugacy ξ = λρ(λ)^{-1} versus ξ = λℓ_0^{-1}ρ(λ)^{-1}, distinguished by the multiplier p mod 3, with the norm form c²+cd+d² of Z[ω] controlling the multiplier
ideas.modern_name: Twisted conjugacy / nonabelian H^1 of Z/3 acting on SL2(Ẑ), with the Eisenstein norm form

ideas.what: Recovery of the multiplier p from ξ alone (p = ∓1/D), up to sign from the SL2 image, exactly from the GL2 image of λ
ideas.modern_name: Determination of λ (cyclotomic part) from f in GT-hat
ideas.usually_credited_to: The fact that λ is determined by f is standard in Drinfeld/Ihara theory

missed.claim: At the congruence (SL2(Ẑ), Γ(2)) level, the GT-type loop equation reduces to the cyclotomic multiplier being the inverse of a value of the Eisenstein norm form c²+cd+d² on the parameter λ. Also, the twisted-conjugacy class of ξ is determined by χ mod 3. This is an explicit description of the image of GT-type solutions in the congruence completion. I do not recall it being stated in this form in the GT literature.
missed.quote: cette équation est relativement anodine et très simple — elle dit simplement que pD = 1, où D = c²+d²+cd dans le premier cas
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor but explicit computation of the 'congruence shadow' of GT-hat, relevant to work on GT actions on modular / congruence quotients. It is probably reconstructible by specialists.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful, correct but elementary computation pushing the loop equation to SL(2,Ẑ). The Eisenstein norm form and the mod-3 dichotomy are a pleasant explicit detail, but specialists would find them unsurprising and easily rederived.
transcription_corrections: '348' at the top is the manuscript's own page number (in the 293-650 range), not an inserted word.
'ρ ≡ -1 (3)' in (102), and 'ρ = χ(u) ≡ 1 ou ≡ -1', should read p (the multiplier p = 2σ+1), not ρ.
'γ ≡ -1 (3)' / 'γ ≡ 0' should be r (or σ), with p = 2r+1, consistent with the previous page.
'h_0^{-1}' in ξ = λ h_0^{-1} ρ(λ)^{-1} should be ℓ_0^{-1} (l_0), as on the previous page; likewise in the parenthetical g = λ_0 ℓ_0^{-1} ρ(λ_0)^{-1}.
'π̂_{0,3}' is a hat-Π_{0,3} (profinite π_1 of P^1 minus 3 points); 'l'un de' is probably 'l'image de π̂_{0,3}'.
